A.subject: Physics
A.text: A uniform rod of mass m and length L with a particle of mass m attached at its one end is released from horizontal position. The other end of rod is hinged. If Young's modulus of rod is Y, then total elongation in rod when it becomes vertical is (A is cross-sectional area of rod and ω is its angular velocity when rod becomes vertical)
A.sol_text:
Using work energy theorem
1/2 Iω² + 1/2 m(ωl)² = mg(L/2) + mgl
1/2 (ml²/3)ω² + 1/2 mω²l² = 3/2 mgl
ml²ω² 2/3 = 3/2 mgl
ω = √(9g/4l) ⇒ ω = (3/2)√(g/l)

Using work energy theorem
1/2 Iω² + 1/2 m(ωl)² = mg(L/2) + mgl
1/2 (ml²/3)ω² + 1/2 mω²l² = 3/2 mgl
ml²ω² 2/3 = 3/2 mgl
ω = √(9g/4l) ⇒ ω = (3/2)√(g/l)

T = (m/L)ωx(L - x + x/2) + (m + m/L x)g + mω²L
= (m/L)ω²(Lx - x²/2) + m(ω²L + g) + (m/L)gx

Stress = T/A = (mω²/A)(x - x²/(2L) + L + g/ω² + (g/ω²)·(x/L))

Strain at this location = dl/dx

dl/dx = (mω²)/(YA)(x - x²/(2L) + L + g/ω² + (g/ω²)·(x/L))

∫ dl = (mω²)/(YA) ∫ (x - x²/(2L) + L + g/ω² + (g/ω²)·(x/L))dx

Δl = (mω²L)/(YA)(4/3 L + 3g/(2ω²))

A.text: A bar AB of length L having non-uniform cross-section is fixed at end A and hanging in vertical plane. Bar is subjected an axial force F at end B as shown in figure. If longitudinal stress have same value on all section of rod. Then its area of cross-section at a distance x from end B is (Given cross sectional area at B is S and density of wire is ρ)
A.sol_text:
Consider a strip of length dx at a distance x from lower end. Let A be area at PQ and A + dA be the area at section RS

FBD of strip

Here σ is stress
And σ = F/S

Now σ(A + dA) = σA + ρAdxg

dA/A = (ρg/σ)dx

⇒ ∫_S^A (dA/A) = (ρg/σ)∫_0^x dx

⇒ ln(A/S) = (ρg/σ)x

A/S = e^(ρgx/σ)

⇒ A = Se^(ρgS/F)x

A.text: Two sources of sound A and B produces the wave of 350 Hz, they vibrate in the same phase. The particle P is vibrating under the influence of these two waves. ⇒ F = (2Tm)/(d²ρ)

A.text: An ideal gas of molar mass M is contained in a very tall vertical cylindrical vessel in the uniform gravitational field in which the free fall acceleration equals g. A.text: n moles of an ideal gas undergoes a process A → B as shown in the figure. The maximum temperature of the gas during the process will be

B.text: Two wires of the same material (Young's modulus Y) and same length L but radii R and 2R respectively are joined end to end and a weight W is suspended from the combination as shown in the figure. The elastic potential energy in the system is (NW²L)/(40πR²Y). Find the value of N.
B.sol_text:
F = W, P.E. = (1/2)(Stress)²/Y · (Volume)

∴ For 1st wire,
Stress = W/(4πR²)
And E₁ = (1/2) · (W²)/(16π²R⁴) · (1/Y) · 4πR² · L = (W²L)/(2.4πR²Y)

For 2nd wire,
Stress = W/(πR²)
∴ E₂ = (1/2) · (W)/(πR²) · (W)/(πR²) · (1/Y) · πR² L = (W²L)/(2πR²Y)

∴ E = E₁ + E₂ = (1/2) · (W²L)/(πR²Y) · [1 + 1/4] = (5W²L)/(8πR²Y)

⇒ E = (25W²L)/(40πR²Y)

∴ N = 25

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text:
Consider the following statement.
I. Electron density of benzene ring in
[benzene with CH₃] is more than that in [benzene with C(CH₃)₃]

II. [benzene cation] more stable than [cyclohexadiene cation]

III. [benzene anion] more stable than [cyclohexadiene anion]

Which of the following is correct?
(1) I & II only
(2) II & III only
(3) Only I
(4) I & III only
A.sol_text:
Answer: (4)
Solution:

[Toluene structure: benzene-CH₃]

I. has higher electron density as number of hyperconjugable H-atom is 3, but in [benzene-C(CH₃)₃] number of hyperconjugable H-atoms = 0.

[Benzene with tert-butyl group structure: benzene-C(Me)₃]

II. Positive charge on more electronegative atom is less stable and hence
[benzene cation] > [cyclohexadiene cation]

III. Negative charge on more electronegative atom is more stable and hence
[benzene anion] > [cyclohexadiene anion]

A.sol_text:

Solution:

The compound A with structure shown as fused bicyclic ring system (naphthalene-like) undergoes ozonolysis and reduction with Zn/H₂O.

Starting material A (shown as bicyclic structure with one double bond) reacts with:

(ii) Zn/H₂O - reductive workup

This produces 2 mol of product with structure: O=C-CH₂-CH₂-C(=O)-CH₂-C(=O)
(a triketone/malondialdehyde type product)

The structure that fits this reaction pattern is option (2), which shows a bicyclic compound with conjugated double bonds (naphthalene or similar fused ring system with partial unsaturation) that when cleaved by ozonolysis and reduced gives the dialdehyde/triketone product shown.

(2) B₂H₆ / THF, and alkaline H₂O₂
(3) O₃ / H₂O / Zn dust

Hydroboration of alkenes by B₂H₆/THF followed by oxidation in presence of alkaline H₂O₂ results in the addition of H₂O according to anti Markovnikov's rule.

                —(ii) H₂O₂ / OH⁻

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text:
Major product
On ozonolysis of major product, how many different products are possible?
B.sol_text:
The starting material is a cyclobutane with two vinyl groups (C=C) at opposite positions and two hydrogen atoms at the other positions.

Step 1: Reaction with conc. H₂SO₄/D, NBS, and alc. KOH
The cyclobutane undergoes ring-opening and rearrangement through a carbocation intermediate. The acid-catalyzed ring opening of the cyclobutane followed by NBS bromination and then elimination with alcoholic KOH produces a diene product.

The mechanism involves:
- H⁺-catalyzed ring opening of cyclobutane
- Formation of a resonance-stabilized carbocation
- Ring closure to form a six-membered ring with multiple double bonds
- NBS performs allylic bromination
- alc. KOH eliminates HBr via E2 mechanism

The major product is 1,2,4,5-tetramethylbenzene (durene) with a bromine substituent, which after elimination gives 1,2,4,5-tetramethylbenzene.

Step 2: Ozonolysis of the major product
The major product is 1,2,4,5-tetramethylbenzene (a substituted benzene with four methyl groups at positions 1,2,4,5).

Upon ozonolysis:
- O₃ attacks the C=C double bonds
- DMS workup cleaves the ozide
- For a monosubstituted or disubstituted benzene system after ozonolysis

Since the major product is 1,2,4,5-tetramethylbenzene:
- Ozonolysis cleaves the aromatic ring at one position
- This can occur at one of two different C=C bonds in the resonance structures
- Due to symmetry, there are 2 different possible cleavage products

The two products would be:
1. A dicarbonyl compound from cleavage at one position
2. Another dicarbonyl compound from cleavage at a different equivalent position

Answer: 02.00 (2 different products are possible)
B.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

B.text: Let y = f(x) is a parabola of the form y = x² + ax + 1 and its tangent at the point of intersection of y-axis and parabola also touches the circle x² + y² = r². It is known that no part of parabola is below x-axis. If radius of circle when 'a' attains its maximum value is 1/k, then value of k² is equal to _______.
B.sol_text:
Since no point of parabola is below x-axis, i.e., x² + ax + 1 > 0 ∀ x ∈ ℝ for which D ≤ 0
⇒ a² - 4.1 ≤ 0 ⇒ -2 ≤ a ≤ 2
∴ max. (a) = 2
When max. (a) = 2, then equation of parabola is
y = x² + 2x + 1 ...(1)
Parabola (1) will cut y-axis at the point where x = 0, then from (1), y = 1
∴ Parabola (1) cuts y-axis (0, 1)

Also, from (1)
dy/dx = 2x + 2
∴ Slope of tangent at (0,1) to the curve is
m = (dy/dx)_(0,1) = 2 × 0 + 2 = 2
∴ Equation of tangent at (0,1) to the parabola (1) is
y - 1 = 2(x - 0)
∴ y = 2x + 1 ...(2)

Now when the tangent (2) touches the circle x² + y² = r²,
Then length of perpendicular from centre O(0,0) to the tangent (2) = radius of circle 'r'
⇒ |0 - 0 + 1|/√(2² + (-1)²) = r
⇒ r = 1/√5 = 1/k (given)
⇒ k = √5
Then value of k² = 5
